- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after a recent price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment is positive — apply a “cool-down” correction by subtracting 1-2% from forecast peak.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust — apply a downward bias correction starting from day 10+ of forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1-3% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1-2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment extremes — cap forecast at ±5% of recent 7-day moving average to avoid volatility overfitting.
